story_text.value:
If I'm abusing Show HN feel free to downvote (I know this blurs the line between a job post and a Show), but genuinely just trying to get some feedback from other engineers / engineering leaders on an approach we're trying here @ DocLoop re: engineering interviewing.

TLDR: Now that coding is no longer at a premium my thesis is that alignment is more precious than ever.... this is my optimistic attempt at trying to build something that achieves a _little_ bit of it. It's a compromise between the challenges everyone hates taking and _something_ that a recruiting team can use to get some meaningful signal amidst the sea of AI submissions that come.

Definitely open to critique!

story_text.value:
Hello HN,

I've been working on a new Web engine, build around two ideas:

- use formal methods from day one. - make it modular.

The modularity is orientated towards the following goals:

- enabling shipping anywhere, including on IOS in the EU as per Apple’s guidelines. - only write code for stuff the OS or application platform cannot do for you: keep binary size to a minimum and achieve native performance. - developer choice: bring what you want, and only build what you need.

For example you can choose a JS engine like v8 or Boa, or just bring your own. The entire graphics pipeline consists of components whose implementation can be swapped-out, with currently a relatively fast path on Mac integrating with Core Animation and a slower cross platform path.

Project is at https://github.com/gterzian/formal-web

Intro essay at: https://medium.com/@polyglot_factotum/how-i-am-building-a-we...

Please let me know what you think.

title.value: Show HN: A malleable and formally verified Web engine

story_text.value:
My friend and I are Neovim nerds, and every so often our Neovim setups would throw errors. What did we do? We talked to each other and solved it. It was never Neovim’s fault.

We think the same way about harnesses. If you don’t like something, you shouldn’t have to call a trillion-dollar company; you should be able to fix it yourself. If you want something custom, you shouldn’t have to keep spamming some discussion thread; you should be able to write it yourself.

And more than anything, it should be simple and fast, and your computer shouldn’t scream OOM. That’s the inspiration behind uji.

I hope you all love it!!!

title.value: Show HN: Uji – Gentoo of Coding Agents

story_text.value:
Hello all,

Ive been building Fabivo, a free furniture planner that runs in the browser. You sketch it simply by drawing it, (by far my favorite feature of this app), clicking for boards or just selecting some starting designs.

But what i think separates fabivo from others its the image to model ai assistant, which took me a looong time to develop and get some quirks fixed, thanks god latest models are focusing on 3d, thats been helping too!

The photo part is an image to JSON CAD harness: the model returns a parametric furniture model in mm that the app can build and edit. That harness is also what i benchmark, and honestly its the reason the app exists. I wanted to see if a photo could turn into a plan i could take to the saw.

Also finetuned some image models and found interesting stuff, that was a first. My intention was to basically reuse the drawing feature to convert a 2d line sketch from image models like gpt image / nano banana to my parametric model, which "worked", and was actually thinking of using that for prod, but then cheaper/better models at 3d launched, but anyways, i learned a lot!

Im getting better performance from my harness than from plain 3js, tho this is anecdotally and havent actually benchmarked it...

Happy to answer anything, especially about the harness or the cut order.

edit: Adding the numbers, missed them.

17 photos of real furniture, three models, same harness, medium reasoning, same tools. Scored on how close the returned structure and boards are to the gold model, so its my own set. (tho i have a hard time making a good scoring metric... just usually go by look!)

Model (medium reasoning) Avg. time / photo Avg. input tokens / photo Avg. output tokens / photo Avg. tool calls / photo GPT-6.1 Terra 9.5 s 30,409 632 1.06 Claude Sonnet 5.5 13.6 s 50,167 1,592 1.18 Claude Haiku 5.5 34.9 s 66,786 6,658 2.35

Terra was both cheaper per photo and the most consistent to my likings. Sonnet was close on quality, Haiku needed way more tool calls to get there.

title.value: Show HN: Fabivo – Furniture design from a photo to a numbered cut list

story_text.value:
If you've been following along with DeepSeek news you will know they recently added web search capability to the DeepSeek API, where you can use web search under the same API key. It is pretty handy, also super cheap at only $0.75 per 1,000 requests (pretty much as cheap as it gets, one search credit can encompass many responses).

I created a simple TypeScript CLI wrapper around the API for my own agents to use (for open source models and harnesses)

I'm sure most of you could whip this up on your own but it also comes with unit/integration/live/e2e testing, CI checks, changelog, auth handling, linting, sdk wrapper, and a fleshed out readme, potentially saving you a few hours of work + validation. Just need to install, auth, and drop a comment in your 'AGENTS.md' to use `dsearch --help` when agent needs web search.

GitHub: https://github.com/LaishGlenberg/deepseek-search-cli

title.value: Show HN: Simple DeepSeek web search CLI written in TypeScript (fast/cheap)
